parties:
Mozaffar Ahmed ----- Petitioner
Vs.
State and Ors ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in a small compass, is that opposites party No.1 Rashid Ahmed as first party filed a petition under section 144 CrPC stating that the disputed land had been under his long possession and that the second party-petitioner having no right, title or possession was threatening to dispossess him from the land creating an apprehension of breach of peace over possession of the land in question. The officer-in-charge of the local police station submitted a report to the learned Magistrate about an apprehension of breach of peace over possession in the case land. The learned Magistrate drew up a proceeding under section 144 CrPC and upon consideration of the documents of both sides restrained the second party-petitioner from entering into the case land. Subsequently being satisfied that the apprehension of the breach of peace over possession of the land continued to exist, the learned Magistrate under his order dated 27-2-97 converted the said proceeding into one under section 145 CrPC, attached the disputed land and appointed Officer-in-charge of the local police station receiver of the property. Being aggrieved by this order of the learned Magistrate, the present petitioner, namely, the second party moved the learned Sessions Judge under section 435/439A of the Criminal Procedure Code being Criminal Revision No. 27 of 1997 and the learned Sessions Judge under his order dated 3-3-97 summarily rejected the revisional application holding that the Magistrate was perfectly justified in passing the order of attachment and appointment of the receiver as he was satisfied that there was an apprehension of breach of peace over possession in the case land. 

 3. Faruque Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that there is a civil litigation over the disputed property because of which jurisdiction of the Magistrate to pass an order under section 144 or under section 145 CrPC is ousted. He submits that the present opposite party No. 1 Rashid Ahmed in his capacity as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 290/94 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the disputed property with a prayer for temporary injunction and that the civil Court on hearing his application rejected the prayer for temporary injunction over the case land. Mr. Farque Ahmed further submits that the present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 262/96 in the local civil Court for declaration of his title to and confirmation of his possession in the case land. The learned Advocate submits that both these title suits are pending over the case land and, in this view of the matter, it is beyond the jurisdiction of the learned Magistrate to pass an order under section 144 or 145 CrPC. 

 4. It is admitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that a competent civil Court is yet to decide the question of title or possession over the disputed land and, in other words, the civil Court is yet to pass an order of injunction or a decree in favour of either party. In this connection we may refer to the decision in the case of Nader Ali Sheikh vs. State reported in 35 DLR 180 wherein it was held that pendency of a civil suit is no bar to the institution of a proceeding under section 145 of the CrPC if the Magistrate is satisfied that there is an immediate apprehension of breach of peach over possession of the disputed land. In the case of Jobeda Khatun vs. Mamtaz Begum 45 DLR (AD) 31 it was held by their Lordships that the law on the subject is fairly well settled when a civil suit is filed before proceeding under section 145 CrPC is drawn up. If a civil Court is already seized with the subject-matter of dispute and has also passed an order regulating possession thereof or in a case in which a decree for possession has been granted or a decree for permanent injunction has been granted, the jurisdiction of a Magistrate under section 145 CrPC is ousted, the only saving being that action can be taken under section 107 and 151 CrPC to prevent breach of peace, but no order by a Criminal Court for attachment of the property under section 145 CrPC can validly be made. In the instant case though two civil suits, instituted before the drawing up of the proceeding under section 145 CrPC, are pending, the civil Court has not passed any order regulating possession of the case land, nor a decree for possession or permanent injunction has been granted. In this view of the matter, the jurisdiction of the Magistrate to act under section 145 CrPC is not ousted. Under the order dated 27-2-97 the learned Magistrate converted the proceeding under section 144 CrPC into one under section 145 CrPC appointed a receiver attaching the disputed property under the second proviso to sub-section (4) of section 145 and directed the parties to put in written statements of their respective claims. In this view of the matter, the learned Sessions Judge was perfectly justified in rejecting the revisional application holding that the learned Magistrate acted within his jurisdiction in passing the order dated 27-2-97 on being satisfied about an apprehension of breach of peace over possession of the case land.
